user.title: EV Smart Charger Setup - Step {step}/{total_steps}
user.description: Set a name for this charger entry. The integration exposes the public charging profiles `manual` and `solar_surplus`; Night Smart Charge and Boost Charge are controlled through dedicated helper entities after setup.

data_description.name: Friendly name shown in Home Assistant.

entities.title: Charger Entities - Step {step}/{total_steps}
entities.description:
Map everything about the charger. Every field is required unless it says optional.

**On/off control — pick ONE:**
- **Switch** (most wallboxes): map the switch and leave both buttons empty.
- **Start / Stop buttons** (e.g. Growatt THOR): leave the switch empty and map both buttons.

**Charging power and charger current:** map the total power, and the current of one phase, in the first field. If you have one sensor per phase, map L1 there and L2/L3 in the optional fields; with current per phase the integration sees how many phases the car charges on.

data_description.ev_charger_switch: Switch entity that turns the charger on or off. Leave empty if your charger exposes start/stop buttons instead.
data_description.ev_charger_start_button: Optional. For chargers that expose start/stop buttons instead of a switch (e.g. Growatt THOR). Map both buttons and leave the switch empty.
data_description.ev_charger_stop_button: Optional. Pressed to stop charging when the charger is controlled with buttons.
data_description.ev_charger_status: Reports the charger state (e.g. charging, available, finished). Used for the plugged-in, idle and finished status.
data_description.charging_power: Measured charging power in W or kW: the total, or phase L1 when L2 and L3 are mapped below. Needed to compute the house consumption.
data_description.charging_power_l2: Only when the first charging power field holds L1.
data_description.charging_power_l3: Only when the first charging power field holds L1.
data_description.fuse_charger_current: Measured charger current in A. One phase (all phases carry the same current), or L1 when L2 and L3 are mapped below. A sensor with L1/L2/L3 attributes (e.g. OCPP current_import) is read per phase.
data_description.fuse_charger_current_l2: Map L2 and L3 to see how many phases the car charges on.
data_description.fuse_charger_current_l3: Map L2 and L3 to see how many phases the car charges on.

solar.title: Solar Panels - Step {step}/{total_steps}
solar.description: Map the solar production in W or kW: the total, or phase L1 with L2 and L3 in the optional fields (they are added up).

data_description.fv_production: Solar production in W or kW: the total, or phase L1 when L2 and L3 are mapped below.
data_description.fv_production_l2: Only when the field above holds L1.
data_description.fv_production_l3: Only when the field above holds L1.

battery.title: Home Battery - Step {step}/{total_steps}
battery.description: Map the home battery. Both fields are required: the battery power is part of the computed house consumption, also when the battery is only shown.

data_description.soc_home: Home battery state of charge in percent.
data_description.battery_power: Signed battery power in W — NEGATIVE = discharging, POSITIVE = charging. If your sensor reports the opposite sign, invert it with a template sensor (see the README).

pv_forecast.title: Solar Forecast - Step {step}/{total_steps}
pv_forecast.description: Solar forecast for today and tomorrow, in kWh. Both are required; they are shown on the dashboard and kept for future planning.

data_description.pv_forecast: Sensor with today's solar production forecast in kWh.
data_description.pv_forecast_tomorrow: Sensor with tomorrow's solar production forecast in kWh (e.g. sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_tomorrow).

dashboard.description: Auto-generate a Lovelace dashboard preloaded with every helper entity from this integration. The dashboard will appear in the sidebar as 'EV Smart Charger' with a glass-style UI inspired by iOS 18. Zero YAML, zero configuration.

data_description.create_dashboard: When enabled, a dedicated Lovelace panel-mode dashboard is created at /ev-smart-charger and registered as a sidebar entry.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Wallbox Model - Step {step}/{total_steps}
reconfigure.description:
Choose how your wallbox adjusts the charging current.

**Tuya** — current is set only to fixed values (6, 8, 10, 13, 16, 20, 24, 32 A); to lower it the wallbox is switched off and on (a few seconds' pause). This is the default and works with the most common wallboxes — pick it if unsure.

**Generic** — accepts any whole-ampere value (6, 7, 8, … 32 A) via a `number` entity: finer control and, when decreasing, the current drops live without interrupting the session.

data_description.charger_model: Tuya = fixed steps (default). Generic = 1 A steps for non-Tuya wallboxes that expose the current as a number entity.

features.title: What do you have? - Step {step}/{total_steps}
features.description:
Tell the integration what your installation looks like. Only the steps and fields that apply to you are shown afterwards, and you can change these answers later from the integration's options.

**Solar panels** — enables solar-surplus charging and the solar forecast step.

**Home battery** — asks for the home battery sensors and creates the battery settings (minimum SOC, battery support, daily home targets).

**Load balancing** — keeps the house below the main fuse while the car charges. *Display only*: the integration works out what load balancing should do and shows it on the dashboard, but never changes the charger (for example when an external load balancer is in charge). *Display and adjust*: the integration also lowers, pauses and raises the charging current itself.

data.home_battery_control: Let EV Smart Charger use the battery

data_description.has_solar: Turn off if the house has no solar panels.
data_description.has_home_battery: Turn on if the house has a home battery you want to take into account.
data_description.home_battery_control: Turn off when the battery has its own control (for example an AI optimiser). It is then only shown on the dashboard: charging never waits for it, never draws from it and the battery settings are hidden.
data_description.load_balancing: None, display only, or display and adjust.

meter.title: Electricity Meter - Step {step}/{total_steps}
meter.description:
Map your electricity meter. Every field is required except grid available. These sensors are used in every setup: the surplus, the computed house consumption and the load balancing all come from them.

The current per phase gets its direction from the import and export power: a phase that sells to the grid leaves extra room for charging.

data_description.main_fuse_size: The rating of your main fuse per phase. Used by load balancing (display only, or display and adjust).
data_description.grid_import: One sensor in W or kW: positive when buying from the grid, negative when selling (for example the net sensor made for the Energy dashboard).
data_description.fuse_grid_import_l1: Power bought from the grid on this phase (0 while selling).
data_description.fuse_grid_import_l2: Power bought from the grid on this phase (0 while selling).
data_description.fuse_grid_import_l3: Power bought from the grid on this phase (0 while selling).
data_description.fuse_grid_export_l1: Power sold to the grid on this phase (0 while buying).
data_description.fuse_grid_export_l2: Power sold to the grid on this phase (0 while buying).
data_description.fuse_grid_export_l3: Power sold to the grid on this phase (0 while buying).
data_description.fuse_grid_current_l1: Current through the main fuse on this phase, in A. May be unsigned.
data_description.fuse_grid_current_l2: Current through the main fuse on this phase, in A. May be unsigned.
data_description.fuse_grid_current_l3: Current through the main fuse on this phase, in A. May be unsigned.
data_description.fuse_grid_voltage_l1: Voltage on this phase, in V.
data_description.fuse_grid_voltage_l2: Voltage on this phase, in V.
data_description.fuse_grid_voltage_l3: Voltage on this phase, in V.
data_description.grid_available: Optional. Binary sensor reporting grid availability (on = grid present, off = grid lost). When off, night charging from the grid stops so it does not drain the home battery during an outage.

data_description.car_connection: Sensor that shows whether the charging cable is connected, e.g. sensor.my_car_charging_connection_status. This car becomes the active car when it reads connected and the car is home.

error.invalid_battery_capacity: Battery capacity must be between 10 and 200 kWh.
error.invalid_domain: Entity must belong to the `number` or `input_number` domain.
error.fuse_phase_reading_required: Map at least the meter current or the meter import power for this phase.
error.fuse_charger_current_required: Map the charger current (a sensor with L1/L2/L3 attributes, or per-phase sensors).
error.charger_control_required: Map either a charger switch or both the start and stop charging buttons.
error.car_name_exists: Another car already has this name.
error.car_name_reserved: This name is used by the Guest profile.

disabled_helpers.title: Some EV Smart Charger helper entities are disabled
disabled_helpers.description: {count} helper entit(y/ies) of "{entry_title}" are disabled in Home Assistant ({entities}). EV Smart Charger started in degraded mode, using safe defaults for the disabled values. This is tolerated, but disabling entities is not a supported way to turn features off. Re-enable them under Settings → Devices & services, or wait for per-feature opt-out toggles (issue #24). This notice clears automatically on the next clean start.
